{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"In December, the largest Marks & Spencer food hall outside the UK will open at Dubai Festival City with an area of 15,327 sq ft.","supported":true,"evidence":[1]},{"claim":"The store will carry the full M&S Food range, including more than 3,500 core products and 500 locally sourced products.","supported":true,"evidence":[1]},{"claim":"Fresh M&S flowers will make their international debut in the region for the first time.","supported":true,"evidence":[2]},{"claim":"The Middle East will get its first M&S Patisserie.","supported":true,"evidence":[3]},{"claim":"The store will have sushi, rotisserie chicken, pizza, and a coffee shop counters.","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"The store offers a wide range of ready meals and products for convenient shopping.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,5,7]},{"claim":"The partnership between Al-Futtaim and M&S has lasted nearly 30 years.","supported":true,"evidence":[8,10]},{"claim":"The first M&S store in Dubai opened in 1998.","supported":true,"evidence":[9]},{"claim":"The new food hall will set a new benchmark for food retail in the UAE.","supported":true,"evidence":[7,8]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"In Sharjah, gatherings in open desert areas are allowed.","supported":true,"evidence":[0,1,3,8,9]},{"claim":"Sharjah Police clarified that residents can freely visit and gather in open desert areas if they comply with traffic rules and restrictions in certain zones.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,3,8,9,10]},{"claim":"Being simply present with friends or family in the desert is not a reason for a fine.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,6,9]},{"claim":"Brigadier Khalid Al Kay stated that entry into the desert is not prohibited, but some areas have restrictions marked by signs.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,3,8,9]},{"claim":"Police will investigate the reasons for fines issued to five vehicles to clarify the details.","supported":true,"evidence":[4,5,6,9]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"From January 1, 2027, the UAE will introduce two-year car registration.","supported":true,"evidence":[0,1,6]},{"claim":"Owners of light vehicles can apply for two-year registration instead of annual renewal if their vehicle meets three conditions.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,4]},{"claim":"The vehicle must be new at first registration.","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"The vehicle must be no older than six years.","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"The vehicle must be owned by an individual (not a company or legal entity).","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"New rules prohibit registration of right-hand-drive vehicles for road use in the UAE.","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"Registration may be cancelled if the vehicle has serious damage or does not meet safety requirements.","supported":true,"evidence":[5]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"Dubai will link all traffic signals to an AI-run control centre by 2027.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,2,4,5]},{"claim":"The control centre is located in Al Barsha.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,4]},{"claim":"The AI system will predict and prevent traffic jams, reducing congestion at signals by at least 10%.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,2,6,8]},{"claim":"The connection of all traffic signals to the centre is planned to be completed by early 2027.","supported":true,"evidence":[2,5]},{"claim":"The system will analyze traffic movement via cameras and dynamically adjust signal timings according to road conditions.","supported":true,"evidence":[2,6,7]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"The UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention announced an improved system for sick leave certificate attestation in healthcare facilities in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, and Fujairah.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,3]},{"claim":"Now healthcare facilities, not patients, submit attestation applications, reducing bureaucracy.","supported":true,"evidence":[1,2,3]},{"claim":"There is an automatic link between attestation and approval of sick leaves that speeds up the process for employees of the federal and local governments of these emirates.","supported":true,"evidence":[3,4]},{"claim":"The application process for leave for patient companions has also been simplified.","supported":true,"evidence":[4,5]},{"claim":"The Ministry links these changes to the UAE Government’s Zero Bureaucracy program and aims to improve the quality and speed of government services.","supported":true,"evidence":[5,6,8]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"In the UAE, 15 criteria have been approved for the practical driving test.","supported":true,"evidence":[0,2,5]},{"claim":"The minimum passing score is 75%.","supported":true,"evidence":[0,3,23,32]},{"claim":"The criteria include vehicle control, parking, maneuvering on slopes, maintaining distance, and correct use of mirrors and signals.","supported":true,"evidence":[5,6,7,9,10,19,20,12]},{"claim":"The exam is conducted by licensing authorities or accredited driving schools.","supported":true,"evidence":[4]},{"claim":"Any candidate scoring less than 75% is considered to have failed and is given a new date to retake the test.","supported":true,"evidence":[3,23]},{"claim":"A candidate can also fail the exam if they create a dangerous situation even if they have a sufficient score.","supported":true,"evidence":[24]}]}

{"supported":true,"reason":"All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.","claims":[{"claim":"In Dubai, a 1650-meter tunnel on Al Khaleej Street has been opened.","supported":true,"evidence":[0,1,2]},{"claim":"The tunnel connects the Deira district with the intersection of Al Khaleej Street and Al Wuheida Street.","supported":true,"evidence":[2]},{"claim":"The tunnel has three lanes in each direction and a capacity of 12,000 vehicles per hour.","supported":true,"evidence":[3]},{"claim":"The tunnel is part of the Al Shindagha Corridor Development Project, which will improve transport connectivity and reduce travel time in the area to 16 minutes by 2030.","supported":true,"evidence":[3,4,5]},{"claim":"The tunnel decoration uses a mosaic of 35 million pieces created by artist Maryam Al Hathboor.","supported":true,"evidence":[8] }]}
